signals.quote: VALUES CERTIFICATIONS Global Recycled Standard BCorp Bluesign Outdoorwear brand Patagonia uses lower-impact materials and traces most of its supply chain.
signals.note: Patagonia holds certifications for Global Recycled Standard, BCorp, and Bluesign.

signals.quote: Patagonia Works has been a Certified B Corp since December of 2011, and since then have dedicated themselves to upholding their core values.
signals.note: Patagonia has been a Certified B Corp since December 2011.

signals.quote: To hold ourselves accountable, we have set goals aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi).
signals.note: Patagonia has set greenhouse gas emission reduction goals that are aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative.

signals.quote: Near-Term – FY2030: · Reduce absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions 80%. · Reduce absolute Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods and services, upstream transportation and distribution, business travel and downstream transportation and distribution 55%.
signals.note: Patagonia aims to reduce its Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 80% and Scope 3 emissions by 55% by fiscal year 2030.

signals.quote: Some of its supply chain is certified by Fair Labor Association (FLA) and Fair Trade USA including all of the final stage of production.
signals.note: Parts of Patagonia's supply chain, including the final production stage, are certified by the Fair Labor Association and Fair Trade USA.

signals.quote: Some of its supply chain is certified by FLA Workplace Code of Conduct and Fair Trade USA in the final stage of production.
signals.note: Patagonia's supply chain includes certifications from the FLA Workplace Code of Conduct and Fair Trade USA for its final production stage.

signals.quote: Overall rating: Good Our ratings are based on a scale from 1 (We avoid) to 5 (Great) How we rate Our “Planet” rating evaluates brands based on the environmental policies in their supply chains, from carbon emissions and wastewater to business models and product circularity. Here we rate Patagonia “Good”.
signals.note: Patagonia has an overall 'Good' rating from Good On You, with a 'Good' rating for its planet impact.

signals.quote: Workers’ rights are central to our “People” rating, which assess brands’ policies and practices on everything from child labour to living wages and gender equality. Here we rate Patagonia “Good”.
signals.note: Patagonia received a 'Good' rating for its 'People' impact, which focuses on workers' rights.

signals.quote: The company hired Patagonia understood this at a cost by receiving a complaint for greenwashing accepted by the advertising ethics jury in France.
signals.note: Patagonia received a greenwashing complaint accepted by the advertising ethics jury in France.

signals.quote: The jury considered the matter and accepted the complaint against Patagonia. Indeed, the communication was considered disproportionate.
signals.note: The advertising ethics jury in France found Patagonia's communication to be disproportionate and accepted a complaint against it.

signals.quote: For absolute Scope 3 emissions, we reported a reduction of nearly 35 percent compared with 2019. The main factors contributing to these reductions include improved material efficiency, increased energy efficiency, greater use of renewable electricity, a reduction in on-site coal, and a growing share of recycled materials.
signals.note: H&M Group reported a reduction of nearly 35 percent in absolute Scope 3 emissions compared with 2019.

signals.quote: Also in 2018, factories that supply H&M were named in reports by Global Labour Justice detailing abuse of female garment workers, and more recently in 2023, workers’ rights abuses from the brand’s suppliers in Myanmar came to light.
signals.note: Factories supplying H&M were named in reports detailing abuse of female garment workers in 2018 and workers' rights abuses in Myanmar in 2023.

signals.quote: Fashion retailer H&M and sporting goods chain Decathlon have made commitments to the Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM) to remove sustainability-related labels from their products and websites, and to improve the use of sustainability claims in the future, following an investigation by the Dutch regulator.
signals.note: H&M made commitments to the Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM) to remove sustainability-related labels and improve sustainability claims after an investigation.

signals.quote: In its investigation, ACM found that H&M uses sustainability claims such as “Conscious” and “Conscious Choice,” without explaining what they mean, or providing a description of the sustainability benefits of the products.
signals.note: The ACM found that H&M uses sustainability claims like "Conscious" and "Conscious Choice" without explaining their meaning or providing sustainability benefits.
